mcpDetails.description: Open kuchup.com homepage to inspect public layout and conversion surfaces

content.text:
**I would not put Google display ads on Kuchup, and I would not buy Google Search ads for it yet either.** The site is already built as a conversion product, not as a place that sells attention.

Two different products get called “Google Ads.” They fail here for different reasons.

## Ads *on* the site (AdSense / display)

This fights the product you already have.

The public `/jobs/<slug>` pages are not a blog. They exist so Google and LinkedIn can land a visa-seeking engineer, then the primary CTA is Google OAuth → save to looking-to-apply → company workspace → credits / $29 Full Access. Display units on those pages would bid on the same intent: Indeed, StepStone, Relocate.me, LinkedIn. You would be paying Google a cut to walk people off the page you spent the wrapping funnel to get them onto.

The signed-in board is worse. That surface is a workspace. Ads next to “looking to apply” / MCP / upgrade CTAs look like a content farm and they compete with the only revenue model that already exists (credit packs and Full Access).

There is also a policy/quality problem. AdSense likes original, page-view media. Kuchup’s public listings are thin, frequently 410’d ATS copies with `hiringOrganization: Kuchup`. That is a good SEO/wrapping tactic and a bad AdSense site. Approval is not guaranteed, and even if it lands, RPMs on early job traffic are usually noise next to a $29 conversion.

Brand matters here more than on a recipe site. The buyer is an international engineer deciding whether to trust you with a visa search and a CV. Ad clutter is a trust tax.

## Ads *for* the site (Search / Performance Max)

The economics do not work until the funnel is measured.

“Visa sponsorship jobs Germany” and cousins are some of the most expensive job-seeker keywords on the internet. Your current paid ceiling is roughly **$29 once**, plus small credit packs. A $8–$40 click against that LTV is how you burn a wallet.

You also have no measurement layer in the product today — no gtag / GA4 / Ads conversion tags in the repo — so you could not even tell a cheap click from a paying one.

The acquisition path you already designed is better than Search ads at this stage: public JobPosting pages, `/sitemap-jobs.xml`, LinkedIn wrapping, country pages. That is high-intent traffic that lands on a save CTA instead of a bid auction.

If you ever buy Google Ads, start tiny and only after conversion tracking exists:

1. **Brand terms** (`kuchup`) — cheap insurance once people search the name.
2. A handful of **long-tail** queries (“visa sponsorship backend germany greenhouse”) with a hard CPA cap, landing on `/jobs` or a country page, converting on **save / signup**, not “visited homepage.”
3. Never Performance Max until that is proven. It will spend on generic job traffic.

I would not do even that until Search Console shows the job URLs actually getting impressions. Paid search in front of an unindexed wrapping funnel is guessing.

## How I would think about “ads” on this product

The high-value ad analog is **employer money**, not Google’s network. A company paying to be more visible among visa-positive roles is aligned: the user still wants a job, the payer is the company, you are not renting the page to a competitor. That is a later business, not a snippet to drop in this week.

If the question is “we need some revenue from anonymous browsers,” protect the job-page CTA and keep selling credits / Full Access. A few dollars of AdSense on a save page is the wrong trade.

**Short version:** treat Google as a crawler and a login provider, not as a publisher or a customer-acquisition channel, until organic job URLs and the $29 conversion are clearly working.

</user_query>

mcpDetails.description: Open public jobs hub to see live catalog scale

content.text:
**Yes, but as a niche relocation workspace, not as a European job board.** The current stack can earn a real place with a small, intense audience. It cannot win the market you are standing next to.

## What I actually expect

Kuchup looks like a serious indie product that can become a known tool in visa-SWE circles — Reddit, HN, Telegram groups, people already on relocate.me who hate the spreadsheet. A few hundred to a few thousand users, some $29 unlocks, maybe a habit for people in an active search. That is a place.

I do **not** expect it to become “where you look for sponsored roles in Europe.” LinkedIn, company career pages, and relocate.me already own that job. 57 public visa-positive roles across five countries is not a market. Germany is almost the whole catalog; Ireland is one listing; Portugal is two; the UK hub is empty right now. A relocator who opens `/jobs` and sees that will not trust you as inventory.

That number matters more than the wrapping architecture. People judge a job product by “is my next job here?” Career-page truth is a good claim. Coverage is the claim they test in ten seconds.

## The strategy as stacked today

You are running three bets at once:

1. **Be a better catalog** than syndicated boards (ATS scrape, 6-hour refresh, visa tags).
2. **Get distribution** by wrapping jobs as Kuchup on LinkedIn/Google.
3. **Monetize a workspace** (tracking, credits, MCP, $29 Full Access).

(1) is table stakes, not a moat. Relocate.me already seeded your company list. LinkedIn already has the roles. Your scrape is more honest than Indeed sludge, but honesty does not beat “10× more jobs.” Dupes and bad locations (Adyen San Francisco on the Netherlands list) also tax trust while the catalog is this small.

(2) is clever and fragile. Mapping `hiringOrganization` to Kuchup is a wrapping trick, not a partnership. Your own docs already say LinkedIn may refuse aggregators. If wrapping works, it is the only cheap acquisition that fits a $29 LTV. If they shut it down, country pages plus 57 JobPosting URLs will not carry growth. Google Jobs is even less friendly to a hiring org that is not the employer.

(3) is the actual product. The board, company workspace, and MCP reframe are why someone would stay after they found a role. That is also why $29 one-time plus crypto checkout is a weak company and a fine tip jar: it will not fund inventory expansion, and NOWPayments is friction for the user who would actually pay.

The Free wall (10 companies, 3 roles, 30 credits) only bites if the matched set feels scarce. With ~57 public visa roles, paid inventory may not feel like more of the market — just less friction on a small list.

## Where it *can* win

The user is real. International backend/SWE people targeting DE/NL/UK sponsorship have a painful, months-long workflow: visa noise, ATS tabs, CV variants, a spreadsheet. Nobody loves that. MCP-connected prep is a 2026-native wedge relocate.me does not have.

The place in the market is:

> the short list of companies that actually sponsor, with your decisions and applications attached, and an agent that can work the JD.

Not:

> a Google-scale visa job board funded by ads and $29 unlocks.

That means Germany-first depth beats five-country theatre. MCP and workspace quality beat more marketing pages. Community distribution (visa Discords, relocate.me refugees, “I used this to apply to N26/Zalando”) beats Search ads. Employer-side money is a later chapter, not this one.

## Direct answer

**With the strategies as they currently are — wrapping + thin public catalog + $29/crypto + MCP — I expect a durable niche tool, not a default destination.** That is still a place, if you are honest that the job is “help a few hundred people run a sponsored search,” not “own European visa jobs.”

The failure mode is treating LinkedIn wrapping and country SEO as if they will manufacture a board business on 57 roles. They will not. The success mode is making Germany (then one more country) feel complete for backend/SWE sponsorship, making the workspace the reason to sign in, and using wrapping only as a tap — not as the company.

If you want a single strategy test: would a senior Iranian/Indian/Brazilian engineer in an active Germany search open Kuchup every day *instead of* LinkedIn + a spreadsheet? Today, only if they already bought into the workspace/MCP loop. The catalog alone is not enough.

Daily habit and credit revenue are different products. I’ll look at what actually spends a credit today, then say what would have to change for both to work.

arguments.query: spend credit consume wallet replacement role

content.text:
The daily habit and the credit pack are fighting each other right now. You cannot meter a 57-role Germany list hard enough to make money; you can only train people that Kuchup is empty.

## What a credit buys today

A credit is spent when Kuchup **successfully delivers a replacement role** after someone acts (hide, apply, pin, …), or on the **4th unique public job save** in a day. Looking at a job, tracking it, and opening the ATS are free. MCP is a **separate daily quota**, not the wallet.

So the meter is on **inventory drip**, not on the loop that would replace LinkedIn + a spreadsheet.

That is why people will not buy packs:

- 30 free credits/month is already most of the public visa set.
- After that, spend fails closed: no replacement, no charge, empty board. They do not hit a paywall that feels like “more of the good stuff.” They hit “the catalog is done.”
- `$29` Full Access **turns the meter off**. It is the opposite of a credit business.
- `$0.99` for 10 credits plus NOWPayments is a toy checkout for a visa search.

You cannot sell more tickets to a ride that has already ended.

## Daily open vs money

A senior in an active Germany search opens LinkedIn every day because **new posts appeared** and because **their pipeline lives there**. They open a spreadsheet because **state** lives there (applied, follow-up, visa notes).

Kuchup only becomes that if the home screen is:

- what is new since yesterday at companies I care about
- what I already decided (looking to apply / applied / waiting)
- what died (410 / closed)
- what I can prepare next (one JD, one CV)

None of that should cost a credit. If “see the new FlixBus role” costs money, they stay on LinkedIn. LinkedIn is free and larger.

**Habit is free feed + durable state. Revenue is what happens when they go from browsing to applying harder.**

## If you want credits to sell

Attach the wallet to something they still want after they have seen the list.

| Charge | Don’t charge |
|---|---|
| Extra matched companies beyond the Free 10, once Germany is actually deep | Opening the board |
| Extra public saves from LinkedIn wrapping (4th+ is already this — keep it) | The first look at a new role |
| MCP / reframe / PDF beyond a daily free slice | “Replacement” from an empty catalog |
| A monthly search pass while they are in-market | `$29` forever |

The meter that can work: **more of a dense Germany match set**, and **more application-prep throughput**. The meter that cannot: dripping the same 57 jobs.

Pack math also has to stop looking like a gacha. For this buyer, `50 credits / $4.99` is not a decision. A monthly “I’m searching” price is (`~$15–29/month` while active, credits as overage). Lifetime `$29` plus crypto is how you cap revenue per human at one impulse buy.

## Order of operations

1. **Germany inventory first.** Until “what’s new today” is regularly non-empty for backend/SWE sponsorship, credits will not sell. This is the whole business.
2. **Make the daily loop free and obvious.** New since last visit, pipeline, closed roles. That is the LinkedIn replacement.
3. **Then tighten paid capacity on extras that still deliver.** 11th company, extra saves, extra MCP — only when those extras are real roles and real prep, not a wall in front of nothing.
4. **Kill or demote Full Access as a lifetime cap-remover.** It trains “pay once, never buy credits.”
5. **Card checkout.** Visa-seeking engineers will bounce on crypto for `$4.99`.

If you “just make actions spend more credits” on the current catalog, usage and revenue both go down: they burn the 30, see an empty board, and go back to LinkedIn. The spreadsheet wins because it never runs out of jobs that exist elsewhere.

**Short version:** daily Kuchup = new Germany roles + tracking. Credits = acceleration on a list that still has more to give. Right now you are trying to sell acceleration on a list that is already finished. Fix the list, then the wallet has something to meter.

input.plan:
# Kuchup business plan and business-flow changes

## Thesis

Kuchup’s buyer is an international software engineer (India / Iran / Brazil / similar) in an **active Germany sponsorship search**. They already have LinkedIn. They will pay only if Kuchup is the place they open **every day** for “what is new + where I am in the pipeline,” then pay more when they want to go faster (more companies, more saves, more MCP prep).

It is not a European job board. Public `/jobs` wrapping is **acquisition**, not the product. Relocate.me / LinkedIn keep inventory; Kuchup keeps **state + prep**.

Honest commercial shape: a few hundred in-market users × **~$19/month for 3–9 months**, then churn when they get a job (that churn is success). `$29` lifetime plus crypto packs cannot fund that, and they cap LTV at one impulse buy.

Inventory is a **commercial dependency**, not this implementation slice: 57 visa-positive public roles cannot support a paid “more jobs” story. Do not raise credit burn until Germany is dense enough that a replacement is usually real.

## Current flow (what is broken)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  wrap["LinkedIn or Google job page"] --> save["Save looking-to-apply"]
  save --> board["Capped board 10 companies / 3 roles"]
  board --> drip["Act then replacement costs 1 credit"]
  drip --> empty["Catalog exhausted: no spend, empty board"]
  board --> wall["Banner: Unlock Full Access 29 dollars"]
  wall --> life["plan=full forever"]
  save --> packs["NOWPayments credit packs"]
```

Facts in code today:

- Free: 10 sticky companies, 3 roles/company, 30 monthly credits, 20 MCP writes/day ([`docs/reference/entitlements-and-opportunities.md`](docs/reference/entitlements-and-opportunities.md), [`relocation_jobs/users/entitlements.py`](relocation_jobs/users/entitlements.py)).
- Credits actually spend on **replacement delivery** and **4th+ public save** only ([`relocation_jobs/broadcast/service.py`](relocation_jobs/broadcast/service.py), [`relocation_jobs/web/routes/job_pages.py`](relocation_jobs/web/routes/job_pages.py)). `PDF_RENDER` / `APPLICATION_PACK` / `COMPANY_REFRESH` exist in [`relocation_jobs/credits/policy.py`](relocation_jobs/credits/policy.py) but are **not wired**.
- Paid SKUs: packs `$0.99–$24.99` and **Full Access `$29` one-time** ([`relocation_jobs/payments/catalog.py`](relocation_jobs/payments/catalog.py)). Fulfillment is `set_plan(..., "full")` ([`relocation_jobs/payments/service.py`](relocation_jobs/payments/service.py)).
- Every capacity wall pushes **Unlock Full Access — $29** ([`relocation_jobs/static/js/board-scope.js`](relocation_jobs/static/js/board-scope.js), [`relocation_jobs/static/js/credits.js`](relocation_jobs/static/js/credits.js), job-page copy).
- `CreditGrantKind.SUBSCRIPTION` already exists in [`relocation_jobs/credits/types.py`](relocation_jobs/credits/types.py) and is treated like a recurring grant in [`relocation_jobs/credits/repo.py`](relocation_jobs/credits/repo.py) — unused commercially.

## Target commercial model

| Surface | Free | Searching monthly (~$19) | Credits (overage) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Public catalog + country pages | Yes | Yes | — |
| What’s new on assigned companies, pipeline, closed roles | Yes | Yes | Never charge to *see* |
| Sticky companies | 10 | Uncapped in prefs (Germany-first) | — |
| Public job saves | 3/day | Higher (e.g. 15/day) | 1 credit after the daily free slice |
| MCP write/render | 20/day | Included higher cap (e.g. 200) | Optional overage |
| Application pack (JD + gated reframe + PDF in workspace) | 1–2/month taste | Included allowance | `APPLICATION_PACK` (already costed at 5) |
| On-demand company refresh | No (already Full-only in [`relocation_jobs/web/routes/companies.py`](relocation_jobs/web/routes/companies.py)) | Yes | or 5 credits |

**Stop selling Full Access to new buyers.** Existing `full` / `grandfathered` stay. Optionally map `$29` checkout to **two months of Searching** instead of lifetime `plan=full`.

**Do not sell Google display ads or Search ads.** CAC must stay near zero (wrapping, country SEO, communities). Job-seeker CPC cannot pay back ~$19/month.

**Later (not this plan):** employer-paid placement on the Germany list. That is the real “ads” analog.

## Target user flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  acq["Job page wrap"] --> track["Free: track this role"]
  track --> home["Daily home: new since last visit plus pipeline"]
  home --> prep["Prepare one application"]
  home --> slot["11th company or extra saves"]
  slot --> month["Searching monthly"]
  prep --> over["MCP or application-pack overage"]
  over --> credits["Buy credits"]
  month --> pause["Pause when search ends"]
```

Rules:

1. **Acquisition stays free.** `/jobs/<slug>` CTA is track/save, not checkout. Paywall only after today’s free saves ([`relocation_jobs/web/templates/job_posting.html`](relocation_jobs/web/templates/job_posting.html)).
2. **Habit is free.** New roles on companies they already have, applied/waiting/closed, must never require a credit. Replacement-credit drip is the wrong meter for daily open.
3. **Money is acceleration.** 11th company, extra LinkedIn saves, extra application packs.
4. **Search is seasonal.** Monthly with an obvious pause/cancel. Lifetime access trains one payment and no credits.

## Product / flow changes to apply

### 1. Rewrite the offer (copy + CTAs, no new metering)

- Board strip: **Start Searching — $19/mo** (or Add credits for overage), not Unlock Full Access $29 ([`board-scope.js`](relocation_jobs/static/js/board-scope.js), [`credits.js`](relocation_jobs/static/js/credits.js), [`frontend/src/CompanyCard.jsx`](frontend/src/CompanyCard.jsx)).
- [`homepage/app/pricing/page.tsx`](homepage/app/pricing/page.tsx) and leftover “when paid plans launch” strings ([`relocation_jobs/web/routes/mcp.py`](relocation_jobs/web/routes/mcp.py), how-it-works) must match live checkout.
- Job page empty-wallet copy: buy credits **or Searching**, not Full Access ([`job_pages.py`](relocation_jobs/web/routes/job_pages.py)).

### 2. Free daily loop (habit, still Free)

- Board default: **new since last visit** among sticky companies, then pipeline (looking to apply / applied / closed). Use existing `fetched` / `last_seen` / `user_stats` ([`docs/reference/stats.md`](docs/reference/stats.md)) rather than a new domain.
- Seeing a new role on an already-assigned company does **not** spend `ROLE_REPLACEMENT`. Keep spend only when a **new assignment** is delivered and inventory exists (current `test_action_with_no_replacement_spends_no_credit` behavior stays).
- Do not hide the ATS URL behind a second paywall after they already tracked the role.

### 3. Pricing SKU: Searching monthly

- New checkout kind next to `ORDER_KIND_FULL_ACCESS` in [`relocation_jobs/payments/types.py`](relocation_jobs/payments/types.py) / [`catalog.py`](relocation_jobs/payments/catalog.py).
- Plan: keep `free`; add `searching` (time-bounded) **or** reuse `full` with an `entitled_until` — prefer explicit `searching` so lifetime `full` can remain grandfathered.
- Monthly grant via existing `CreditGrantKind.SUBSCRIPTION` (included save/pack allowance), expiry already distinguished from purchased credits in [`credits/repo.py`](relocation_jobs/credits/repo.py).
- Hide or remap `full_access` SKU for new checkout. Refund path today already reverts `full` → `free` ([`revert_full_access_purchase`](relocation_jobs/payments/service.py)).
- Packs stay as overage; drop or de-emphasize the `$0.99 / 10` mini pack so checkout does not look like a gacha.

NOWPayments can remain the first adapter ([`relocation_jobs/payments/nowpayments.py`](relocation_jobs/payments/nowpayments.py)). Card (Stripe) is the conversion fix for this ICP; add as a second adapter when the SKU exists — do not block the plan change on Stripe.

### 4. Move the meter onto prep (only after Searching exists)

Wire costs that are already in [`OPERATION_COSTS`](relocation_jobs/credits/policy.py):

- `APPLICATION_PACK` (5) when a tailored pack is completed (MCP save + PDF), not on every chat turn.
- Keep `PUBLIC_JOB_SAVE` as overage after the daily free slice.
- Leave `ROLE_REPLACEMENT` at 1 and **do not increase it**. Empty catalog must still spend 0.
- MCP: Searching raises `FULL_MCP_DAILY_REQUESTS`-style cap; Free stays 20/day. Optional: overage spends credits instead of a hard error.

### 5. What not to change in this slice

- Do not add AdSense or Google Ads.
- Do not expand country marketing as if five empty hubs equal a market. Default prefs are already Germany ([entitlements doc](docs/reference/entitlements-and-opportunities.md)).
- Do not treat LinkedIn wrapping `hiringOrganization=Kuchup` as a partnership; it is a tap. If BD refuses the XML feed, organic `/jobs` still feeds the same save CTA.
- Catalog depth (more Germany ATS coverage, dedupe, Adyen-in-NL class bugs) is required for paid “more companies” to feel true, but it is a **separate workstream** from this pricing/flow change.

## Success metrics (prove the loop before pushing spend)

- **Habit:** D1/D7 return; share of Free users who see ≥1 new role in 7 days on their 10 companies.
- **Funnel:** wrap save → looking-to-apply → MCP/PDF → marked applied.
- **Revenue:** conversion at **company-slot wall** and **save overage**, not at “empty replacement.” Searching attach rate; credit-pack revenue should stay secondary.
- **Kill test:** if Germany “new this week” is usually zero, pause paid push and fix inventory.

## Implementation order (after you confirm this plan)

1. Copy/CTA + pricing page (stop selling lifetime).
2. Searching SKU + plan + checkout fulfillment/refund (NOWPayments).
3. Daily “new + pipeline” board home (free).
4. Wire `APPLICATION_PACK` / MCP overage to the wallet.
5. Stripe adapter when Searching conversion is blocked on crypto.
6. Parallel: Germany catalog density (ops/scrape), not mixed into the payment PR.

from relocation_jobs.credits.policy import credit_pack

    ORDER_KIND_CREDITS,

    CheckoutSku,
)


SEARCHING_SKU = CheckoutSku(

    kind=ORDER_KIND_SEARCHING,
    credits=0,
    price_minor=1900,
    currency="USD",
    label="Searching — 30 days",
)

    if key in (SEARCHING_SKU.key, "full_access"):

    pack = credit_pack(key)
    return CheckoutSku(
        key=pack.key,
        kind=ORDER_KIND_CREDITS,
        credits=pack.credits,
        price_minor=pack.price_minor,
        currency=pack.currency,
        label=pack.label,

def update_user_plan(
    user_id: int,
    plan: str,
    *,
    searching_until: str | None = None,
) -> bool:
    now = _utc_now()
    until = None if plan != "searching" else searching_until
    with db_transaction() as conn:
        cur = conn.execute(
            """
            UPDATE users
            SET plan = %s, plan_updated_at = %s, searching_until = %s
            WHERE id = %s
            """,
            (plan, now, until, user_id),
        )
        return cur.rowcount > 0

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best
code is the code never written.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.
3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
4. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

**Bug fix = root cause, not symptom.** A report names a symptom. Before you
edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path (`# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`).

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | Build what's asked, but name the lazier alternative in one line. User picks. |
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |
| **ultra** | YAGNI extremist. Deletion before addition. Ship the one-liner and challenge the rest of the requirement in the same breath. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- lite: "Done, cache added. FYI: `functools.lru_cache` covers this in one line if you'd rather not own a cache class."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."
- ultra: "No cache until a profiler says so. When it does: `@lru_cache`. A hand-rolled TTL cache class is a bug farm with a hit rate."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Never lazy about understanding the problem. The ladder shortens the
solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.

Review diffs for unnecessary complexity. One line per finding: location, what
to cut, what replaces it. The diff's best outcome is getting shorter.

## Format

`L<line>: <tag> <what>. <replacement>.`, or `<file>:L<line>: ...` for
multi-file diffs.

Tags:

- `delete:` dead code, unused flexibility, speculative feature. Replacement: nothing.
- `stdlib:` hand-rolled thing the standard library ships. Name the function.
- `native:` dependency or code doing what the platform already does. Name the feature.
- `yagni:` abstraction with one implementation, config nobody sets, layer with one caller.
- `shrink:` same logic, fewer lines. Show the shorter form.

## Examples

❌ "This EmailValidator class might be more complex than necessary, have you
considered whether all these validation rules are needed at this stage?"

✅ `L12-38: stdlib: 27-line validator class. "@" in email, 1 line, real validation is the confirmation mail.`

✅ `L4: native: moment.js imported for one format call. Intl.DateTimeFormat, 0 deps.`

✅ `repo.py:L88: yagni: AbstractRepository with one implementation. Inline it until a second one exists.`

✅ `L52-71: delete: retry wrapper around an idempotent local call. Nothing replaces it.`

✅ `L30-44: shrink: manual loop builds dict. dict(zip(keys, values)), 1 line.`

## Scoring

End with the only metric that matters: `net: -<N> lines possible.`

If there is nothing to cut, say `Lean already. Ship.` and stop.

## Boundaries

Scope: over-engineering and complexity only. Correctness bugs, security holes,
and performance are explicitly out of scope. Route them to a normal review
pass, not this one. A single smoke test or `assert`-based
self-check is the ponytail minimum, not bloat, never flag it for deletion.
Does not apply the fixes, only lists them.
"stop ponytail-review" or "normal mode": revert to verbose review style.
